safetyNote: Poisonous: Clitocybe rivulosa contains muscarine and can rapidly cause heavy sweating and salivation, breathing difficulty and a slow heart rate. Do not taste or eat it. After suspected ingestion, contact an emergency service or poison centre immediately; treatment may be urgent.

sections.title: Fool's funnel
sections.text: Clitocybe rivulosa is a small, pale grassland mushroom. Its roughly 1–6 cm cap begins convex, then flattens and often develops a shallow central depression; the margin is commonly rolled inward when young and can become wavy. The cap is dry, whitish to cream or buff, with a frosted or floury appearance. Faint concentric zones or cracking may appear with age and dryness, but are not constant.

sections.title: Gills and stem
sections.text: The narrow, crowded gills are white to cream, sometimes greyish-pink with age. They meet the stem directly and may run a short distance down it, rather than remaining free. The short, narrow, pale stem is silky or floury, often downy at its base, with no ring or volva. The spore print is white. Odour is variable and not a safe distinguishing test.

sections.title: Habitat and confusion
sections.text: This species grows in lawns, meadows, roadside verges and parks, sometimes in arcs or fairy rings. In western Europe it is mostly seen from summer into autumn, with local variation. It can grow beside edible grassland species such as Marasmius oreades. The latter normally has more widely spaced gills and a notably tough, pliant stem, but comparison by a single character is unsafe. Names such as C. dealbata have historically been applied to closely similar white clitocybes and are treated as synonyms by some authorities.

sections.title: Muscarine poisoning
sections.text: Muscarine poisoning usually starts quickly, often within 30 minutes to two hours. Sweating, tears, excess saliva, abdominal cramps, vomiting or diarrhoea may accompany a slow pulse, low blood pressure or breathing difficulty from airway secretions. Severe cases need medical assessment; clinicians may use atropine for serious muscarinic effects. A recovery time cannot be promised for an individual, and the pale cap gives no indication that it is safe.

sections.title: About the plate
sections.text: The white-background plate shows a whole specimen, a longitudinal section, the weathered cap from above and the crowded, slightly descending gills from below. It depicts a mature shallow depression and cap zonation, features that vary with age and weather.
